items.name: Avocado Toast
items.description: Smashed avocado on sourdough with pumpkin seeds, cherry tomatoes & arugula, with dressed boiled eggs on the side
ingredients: Eggs, as many as you like (boil extra for the next day)
Salt, black pepper and red chili flakes
Baby sprouted broccoli or other microgreens (optional)
steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Gently lower in as many eggs as you want to eat with a spoon. It's worth boiling extra to have ready for the next day. Turn the heat down to medium, but make sure the water keeps boiling. Set a timer for 8 minutes: 6–7 minutes for a jammy, runnier yolk, or 10 minutes for a hard yolk.
While the eggs boil, take ripe avocados out of the fridge, one per person. Peel, slice and place them in a bowl.
Season with fresh lemon juice, salt, black pepper and red chili flakes. Smush with a spoon and set the bowl aside.
When the timer goes off, lift the eggs out and put them in a large bowl of ice and water. This stops them cooking.
Meanwhile, prepare the toppings. Wash and dry the arugula, a generous handful per person. Slice the cherry tomatoes (about 5 per person) into halves or thirds.

Toast your sourdough. Spread one avocado's worth of smashed avocado over each slice, then sprinkle with roasted pumpkin seeds and extra flaky salt. For an extra kick, add sriracha on top. Rupi always does.
Top with the cherry tomatoes and a generous handful of arugula. If you have baby sprouted broccoli or any microgreens, add those on top too.
Peel the eggs and cut them into quarters. Dress them with salt, pepper, red pepper flakes and a drizzle of olive oil. For a kick, add sriracha or chili oil. Serve alongside the avocado toast.

items.name: Banana Date Porridge
items.description: Hearty winter-warmer — Medjool dates, banana & steel-cut oats. Natural sweetness, no sugar needed
ingredients: ½–1 Medjool date, according to preferred sweetness
steps: Remove the stone from the date. Peel the banana, slice off one third and set aside with a small sliver of the date; these will be used to finish the porridge.

Chop the remaining date and banana very finely. Place in a small pan and pour on 185ml boiling water (Rupi never uses boiling water, and the recipe turns out fine. She puts 185ml of water straight from the tap into the pan). Cook over a low heat until you have a thick, mushy, reasonably smooth paste, stirring regularly and using the back of the spoon to crush any lumps; this should take around 10 minutes. You can also use a stick blender to deal with any stubborn lumps.
While the banana-date mixture is cooking, pour the milk into a bowl, tip in the oats and leave to soak for a few minutes.
When the banana-date mix is ready, add the milk and oats to the pan, bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 12–15 minutes, stirring regularly, until the oats are completely tender.
Slice the remaining third of the banana and finely shred the reserved sliver of date. Serve the porridge in a warmed bowl, topped with the banana slices and dates.

items.name: Turkish Eggs
items.description: Poached eggs on garlicky labneh with chili oil, red pepper flakes, flaky salt & herbs, with buttered sourdough
ingredients: 1 cup labneh (or thick, strained Greek yogurt)
2 tbsp chili oil made with olive oil (such as Calabrian chili oil)
Chopped fresh dill or parsley leaves, for garnish
Sourdough or other bread of your choice, plus butter, for serving
steps: Bring a medium saucepan of water to a simmer over medium heat. Add the 2 tbsp vinegar.
Prepare the labneh: in a small bowl, stir the labneh (or yogurt) together with the garlic. Divide it between two plates, using the back of a spoon to spread it out.

One by one, crack each egg through a fine-mesh sieve. Make sure there is a bowl underneath the sieve to collect the liquid that comes through. This allows the thin, watery part of the white to drain through. This thin, watery part is what turns into wispy white strands in the pot, and we don't want that. Gently tip the egg from the sieve into a small cup or ramekin, taking care not to break the yolk.

When the water is gently simmering, not boiling (boiling or strongly simmering water won't make a proper poached egg, so turn the heat down if it starts to boil), swirl a wooden spoon in the pot to create a little tornado. While the water is swirling, gently slide one egg in, then follow with another. Two eggs max in the pot at one time. Set a timer for 3 minutes (3 minutes for a runny yolk, 3½ minutes for a jammy egg).
When the timer goes off, lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon and rest them on a paper towel, then place them on the labneh. Repeat with the rest of the eggs, 3 per plate.
Once all the eggs are on their plates, scatter over the herbs, drizzle with the chili oil, and sprinkle with red pepper flakes, flaky salt and pepper.
Warm the sourdough (or bread of your choice), butter it and serve alongside.

items.name: Beef & Veggie Power Bowl
items.description: Post-gym power bowl — cumin-turmeric beef bloomed in ghee, peppers, onions, broccoli, spinach, avocado, cilantro-lime & Tajin over jasmine rice. ~60g protein per serving.
ingredients: 1 cup jasmine rice + 1 cup water (1:1 ratio)
1.5 cups precut onion, pepper & chili mix
2 broccoli heads, small florets and sliced stems
steps: Start jasmine rice — rinse 3x until water runs clear. Add to Aroma cooker FIRST, then water. 1:1 ratio. Pinch of salt. Press cook. When it clicks warm, lid stays closed 5 min. Fluff with fork.
Prep everything — cut broccoli into SMALL florets, slice stems thin. Mince garlic. Slice avocado. Chop cilantro. Cut lime. Line everything up near stove.

Bloom spices in ghee — heat large skillet over medium-high. Add ghee. Once it shimmers, add cumin seeds and turmeric. Stir 30 seconds until cumin pops. Add garlic, stir 15-20 seconds. Don't let garlic brown alone.
Brown the beef — add beef, spread flat. Do NOT touch 60-90 seconds to sear. Break up. Season with salt, pepper, and taco seasoning. Cook ONLY until pink is gone. Stop. Do not drain fat.
Add onion-pepper-chili mix — DROP HEAT TO MEDIUM. Cook 3-4 minutes until onions soften and peppers go glossy.
Steam broccoli — add broccoli, light salt, 3 tbsp water. Cover with lid. Cook 3 min on medium. Uncover, cook off excess moisture 1 min. Tender but bright green.
Wilt spinach — heat to low. Add spinach, stir 30-60 seconds until just wilted.
Finish — sprinkle 0.5 tsp chili-lime OR peri-peri (pick one, not both). Taste. Adjust salt.
Build the bowl — rice in bowl, beef & veggie mix on top. Let sit 1 min. Top with sliced avocado, cilantro, squeeze of lime, and Tajin on the avocado. Done.
